result.rationale: The diff adds an unconditional Salesforce token refresh inside the constructor path (fetch to login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token) with `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw new HttpError(...)`. This newly-introduced code runs on every instantiation of SalesforceCalendarService, and reliance on statusText (which can be empty in some HTTP/2 environments and is not a reliable status check) makes transient or nonstandard responses become thrown 400s, affecting the booking path. The mechanism is directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, a refresh-token fetch is now executed unconditionally before creating the jsforce connection. The code checks `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw new HttpError({ statusCode: 400, message: response.statusText });`. Using `statusText` string equality is brittle (it may be empty or differ even when `response.ok` is true), and it will convert any non-exact "OK" into a thrown 400, potentially breaking normal operation whenever this code path runs.
